title: ClipKit Studio feature verification against supplied Word brief

sourceDocument.filename: ClipKit Studio PRD and Agent Build Brief (1).docx

summary: Working reduced MVP; not complete against the full Word PRD. No runtime features were changed by this audit.

statusDefinitions.PASS: The criterion’s behavior has supporting runtime/test/code evidence.
statusDefinitions.PARTIAL: Some behavior exists, but the complete criterion is not satisfied or fully demonstrated.
statusDefinitions.FAIL: A required capability is absent or a reproducible acceptance failure was found.
statusDefinitions.BLOCKED: Live credentials, real speech/footage, a human listening check or client authentication is missing.

features.notes: Core preview, timeline and grouped history work. Missing inspector types, source-bound trim validation and the bare-D shortcut prevent full conformance.
Import/proxy/audio/cuts exist. Restoring baked cut audio is broken; visual filmstrip tool and local STT fallback are absent; live transcription accuracy remains unverified.
Ten native clips, actual previews, retrieval and native index generation exist. General folder packs and complete validation/watch support are missing.
Real Codex, ownership enforcement, revisions, WebSocket sync and crash release work. Patches do not renew expiry; declared MCP parity and two-client verification are incomplete.
Anchored bundles and real resolution work. Timeline pins/range dragging and a proper before/after diff presentation are absent.
The ten native clips highlight and can be selected. Editing uses the right inspector; there is no floating mini inspector or explicit selection-local Ask agent control.
Provider adapters, per-mode takes, record-along, caches and private clone checks exist. Full-script recording, bulk conversion, browser TTS fallback and real voice acceptance are incomplete.
Local grammar and frozen anchors work. The physical speech path is unverified, browser recognition fallback is absent, and destructive/misrecognition handling has gaps.
Shared history, linear undo/redo and latest-turn revert work. Arbitrary revision revert, history-to-timeline highlighting and proper voice attribution are missing.
A playable original-media H.264/AAC export is verified. Only one preset exists; selection controls and a used-license export dialog are absent.

hackathonReadiness.notes: Graphics seed/reset and a recorded real-agent workflow exist; user footage, cached narration and three full rehearsals are absent.
Payload estimates and actual usage are distinguished, but orphan transcripts inflate the baseline after reset.
Local routing is fast after text exists; end-of-speech latency with Fish/microphone was not measured.
Codex works. Claude authentication/scenario and Cursor integration are missing.
Owner/label/banner/activity are shown. Touched IDs are not a dedicated live layer list and there is no agent timeline-position marker.
There is no side-by-side comparison control.
Charcoal UI and tested widths work, but thumbnail cropping and incomplete accessibility review remain.
The full comments/hover/voice specifications are not flawless or fully verified; see the checklist.
Ghost-layer proposals/accept/reject are absent; this was explicitly deferred in the accepted MVP scope.
A demo checklist exists; the requested architecture diagram and finished 30-second real-footage story are not delivered.

criteria.notes: Valid, missing-required-field and wrong-type projects are checked; clip IDs/props are validated by the server.
Patches are atomic, revisioned and cloned before validation; failed transactions leave the snapshot untouched.
A second stale baseRev is rejected with currentRev and no partial changes.
Fresh exact sequence of three edits, two undos, one redo and restart restored Two at revision 6 with six history entries.
The generic composition renders project data, with independent native preview/export frame checks and a seeded browser frame near one second.
Move/trim/split exist, but a source starting at 1000s with a 20s duration was accepted against a five-second source. Source-bound validation is missing.
Descriptor-driven text, multiline, color and number controls exist. Required image/easing controls and inspector sliders are absent; text preview commits on blur.
Eight drag updates generated one revision; one undo restored exact tracks. Inspector fields commit drafts on blur.
Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z worked in Chromium. Bare D did not duplicate as specified. Text-field guards exist.
A real patch was broadcast and observed within the test’s one-second limit.
Server and UI enforce lease ownership, reject human mutations, and permit editing after release. Runtime lease state intentionally replaces persisted agent.status.
Expiry itself works, but an accepted patch at +60s did not extend the lease. Only heartbeat renews it; timeout is also hardcoded rather than configurable.
A deliberately killed child process released the lease and left valid project JSON. This is fault injection, not a simulated successful coding-agent run.

criteria.evidence: HTTP compact-output test; CLI output; MCP transport
criteria.notes: Default summaries omit props and paginate. CLI/MCP have character caps, but the specified large-project/full-layer acceptance case is not covered comprehensively; oversized responses become errors.
Only a compiled native registry is supported. A native entry with an empty license was accepted. General folder-pack/schema/license/rendered-tag validation is missing.
The native JSONL catalog, category index and full schemas generate correctly. Folder-pack add/remove discovery and watching are not implemented.
Description search returned at most five entries and kinetic-title ranked first for a title-intro query.
One selected clip’s schema/defaults are returned; the full catalog is not sent by this command.
Valid native clips render; invalid props and unknown native IDs are rejected.
A real fixture was probed, copied, proxied and audio-extracted with its original hash unchanged. Smaller originals stay below the 720px proxy ceiling rather than being upscaled.
Word-timestamp parsing and sidecars exist, but no live Fish credentials or natural-speech ground-truth fixture was supplied for the 150ms accuracy check. No local Whisper fallback exists.

A structured ten-minute fixture with 1200 filler words produced 52,545 UTF-8 bytes: the uncapped filler candidate array breaks the approximate 12KB target. This is a stress fixture, not a claim about typical speech.
FFmpeg silence detection and a conservative filler grammar exist. The required three-silence/three-spoken-filler accuracy fixture was not available.
Mechanical ripple cuts and baked 30ms fades are tested. Natural-speech waveform/listening acceptance remains unverified without the user clip/listener.
Restoring a cut to four seconds changed video srcIn/dur, but playback still referenced the old three-second baked audio segment at offset zero. Exact audiovisual restoration is broken.
No footage view command or composite filmstrip/waveform/word image operation exists.
Moment/range/layer/element anchor fields and frozen pointer copies are implemented; layer/property anchoring has browser and unit evidence.
Fresh three-comment/two-layer bundle contained exactly two unique layers with a compact payload. Payload guards should still be improved for larger comments.
Open/working/resolved, replies and resolvedRev are stored. The UI shows forward patch operations rather than a true before/after value comparison; resolved revision is not clearly presented.
All three fresh Codex cycles resolved their comments and changed only the targeted text property, preserving every other track/item property.
All ten native clip types were probed across their visible tagged leaf regions, checking labeled hover highlighting and schema-valid property paths. This does not certify arbitrary external packs.
Text/color commits and human history work through the right inspector. There is no floating mini inspector; typing is not previewed until blur/commit.

Canvas-selected property metadata survives moving to the comments panel and is attached automatically. The equivalent Add anchored comment workflow exists; an explicit selection-local Ask agent control does not.
Canvas clicks select the timeline item. Timeline selection sets inspector state, but the canvas outline is hover-only and disappears after leaving the canvas.
A fresh five-line script created five slots and five voice-lane items with target windows.
Mocked-provider tests prove a second request uses cached audio without another TTS call. Live Fish generation remains unverified without credentials.
Countdown, muted record-along preview, teleprompter and multiple takes exist. A real microphone retake/selection/listening test needs human input.
FFmpeg silence trimming is implemented. No speech sample with known leading/trailing pauses was provided to verify speech is preserved.

Within-tolerance takes are automatically stretched, rather than offering a choice. Out-of-range takes retain natural duration with guidance and editable windows, without automatic visual extension/ripple choices.
Private clone creation, retry polling and verified reference checks exist. Refusal of ordinary imported sources is tested; actual cloning and listening require Fish access and a consented sample.
Mode-specific takes and badges work in tests, including an in-flight mode-change guard. Live AI/recorded/cloned playback across all modes still needs provider and microphone verification.
There is no one-click convert-all-AI-to-cloned operation or control.
Loudness normalization and fades exist. The specified 1.5 LU measurement across real narration and crossfade listening check has not been completed; true overlapping slot crossfades are absent.
Captions map from actual take word timings in mocked-provider tests. Mixed real narration timing has not been verified with live STT.

criteria.evidence: Media cached-provider-failure tests; studio provider state
criteria.notes: Existing cached takes survive provider failures. Browser speech-synthesis placeholder playback is absent, so there is no uncached speech fallback.
Push-to-talk code stops tracks on release and has no always-on recognition. Physical microphone capture/indicator behavior has not been verified here.
All listed commands route locally, and typed seek is exercised in Chromium. Spoken recognition-to-action requires Fish access; grammar tests alone do not verify the full speech pipeline.
No real end-of-speech latency measurement is possible without an actual microphone/provider run. Browser Web Speech fallback is absent.
Hovered-anchor capture and real comment-to-agent edits are separately verified. The exact spoken red-and-punchier path has not been run.
Selection, hover, playhead and explicit numeric comment ranges are captured. Loop toggles the entire project, without a stored loop-section range for that part.
Heard text and interpreted action are shown in a toast and agent status has a banner. The specified dedicated bubble/chip speech UI has not been verified with real recognition.
clear all/delete all request confirmation. The specified delete the track command routes to a free-form agent comment, bypassing this local confirmation branch.
Unmatched nonempty text becomes an automatically dispatched agent comment. There is no confidence/repeat gate for unintelligible or unrelated recognition results.
History includes labels/timestamps/operations. Selecting an entry does not highlight the timeline, and voice-originated operations generally receive human/system authors rather than voice.
Linear undo/redo and the latest untouched agent turn work. Arbitrary single-revision revert is absent; ck history revert REV ignores REV and calls latest-turn revert.
Real MP4 export and tone mixing are proven. A full footage+generated-clips+active-spoken-voice project with listening and three cut-point comparisons is not yet verified.
Export passes preview=false and chooses the registered original media variant. Preview uses the proxy variant; a real original-media export was verified.

criteria.evidence: studio Export button; render export credits
criteria.notes: Credits sidecars and bundled notices exist, but there is no export dialog listing licenses of the used clips.
Tarball init is idempotent and preserves existing configuration for Codex/Claude. The literal npm name is unavailable/unpublished here and Cursor rules are absent.
Requirements are checked through ck doctor and runtime fallback binaries, not during init as specified.
The workflow instructions and generated Claude skill are below the approximately 80-line limit.
The declared MCP tools omit several real editing operations, including transcription, cloning, undo/redo/revert and status. Generic CLI op is not MCP parity.

criteria.evidence: Recorded; fresh Codex cycles; claude auth status
criteria.notes: Real Codex edits work, but the full teaser scenario has not been completed by both clients. Claude is installed and not authenticated.
Tracked Git history was scanned for common credential patterns and private/build files; none identified. .env and runtime/build paths are ignored. This is not an exhaustive security guarantee.
Estimated request/tool payload updates during the turn; actual client-reported input/output/cache usage is separately displayed when emitted.

criteria.evidence: HTTP compact-output tests; MCP/CLI guards; Probe.packedTranscript
criteria.notes: Default sample tests pass and transport character caps exist. All-operation/large-project coverage and a consistent byte budget remain incomplete.

Three fresh cycles used estimated payloads of 946, 947 and 940 tokens. This excludes tool definitions/base client context; actual client input was about 91k per turn. The full beyond-base-skill token target is not proven.

criteria.evidence: README method; server state telemetry; Browser.baseline
criteria.notes: The comparison is labeled an estimate and the method is documented. The baseline also counts orphan transcripts after reset/removal, inflating a current-composition comparison.
Data-only prompt instructions and protected patch paths exist. The required adversarial transcript/comment/metadata agent cases were not run; instructions alone are not an injection-proof boundary.

criteria.evidence: server serve hostname; fresh isolated servers
criteria.notes: The HTTP server is bound to 127.0.0.1 and validates browser origins/hosts.
Only registered media IDs are served; raw source paths cannot be inserted through ordinary project_patch, and public asset joins reject escapes.
A source marked imported is refused before clone generation. The app-recording flow includes a rights notice; verified private clone references are enforced.
The full seven-step raw-footage and live hybrid-voice demo has not been completed with the user’s footage/voice, Fish access and both authenticated clients.
An undoable graphics reset and three successful agent edit cycles exist. These are not three full demo rehearsals, and the seed lacks real footage and cached speech/transcripts.
There is no verified complete three-minute run. Fresh agent cycles took 29–37 seconds each; recognition, cloning and export still require end-to-end timing.
No uncaught page errors were observed in the tested paths. This does not establish a clean console throughout the credentialed full demo.
A fresh project offers import/drop, visible library cards and a prompt/command field, plus the explicitly labeled demo fixture.
Visible focus styling is present and exercised. A complete tab-order and contrast review, including low-contrast small text, is not certified.
The major panels fit both widths without page overflow. Portrait thumbnails can crop low-positioned content; exhaustive layout across all voice/export/error states remains incomplete.
